title: Adoption manifest (knowledge/_adoption/MANIFEST.yaml)
description: T89 — every file adoption created or replaced, so it can be undone completely. This is validated on read like any other on-disk artefact, and for a sharper reason than most: rollback deletes files, and a manifest nobody checked is a delete list nobody checked. rollback.ts additionally refuses any path outside `knowledge/`, so even a corrupted manifest cannot reach project code.

path.description: Repo-relative, forward-slashed. Adoption only ever writes under `knowledge/`, but that is checked by rollback.ts's isSafePath rather than by this pattern — deliberately. A pattern here would reject the whole manifest over one bad line, which means a project could not be rolled back at all; the check in rollback refuses that one entry, reports it, and undoes everything else.

action.description: `created` — the file did not exist, so rollback deletes it. `replaced` — it did, so rollback restores `backup` over it. Nothing else: adoption never deletes or moves a legacy file, which is why there is no third action.

backup.description: Repo-relative path of the copy taken before overwriting, under knowledge/_adoption/backup/. null for `created`, required for `replaced` — a `replaced` entry without one would be an undo that cannot undo.

stage.description: Which import stage wrote it, so a partial rollback (one stage, re-run) is possible later without re-reading every file to work out who owns what.
